name: Planable
tagline: Collaboratively draft and approve social posts before manual or API publishing

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 50 posts total (lifetime, not monthly), unlimited workspaces and users; no X publishing
tiers.notes: No time limit and no credit card; the 50-post counter never resets and deleted posts still count.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 60 posts/workspace/month, 4 social pages/workspace, unlimited users, 10 GB media storage

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 150 posts/workspace/month, 10 social pages/workspace, unlimited users, 50 GB media storage

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited posts, pages, labels and campaigns; multi-level approvals, SSO, 100 GB media storage

pricing.freeTierCaps: 50 posts total across unlimited workspaces/users; no reset, deleted posts still count, and X publishing is unavailable
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); subscriptions auto-renew
pricing.hiddenCosts: Pricing is per workspace, not per user. Analytics costs $14/workspace/month or $140/year; Social Inbox/Engagement costs $9/workspace/month or $90/year; an extra-posts add-on raises the cap to 500 posts/month for $49/month or $490/year and applies to all workspaces. Taxes are extra.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Planable, collaboratively draft and approve social posts before manual or API publishing. The hard boundary is high-fidelity previews, approvals, comments, multiple workspaces, and client workflow, plus api access, connector upkeep, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Draft social posts collaboratively, preview them accurately, approve them before publishing manually or through one official API, and retain a searchable content calendar.
requirements: developer application for one social network
whatYouLose: high-fidelity previews, approvals, comments, multiple workspaces, and client workflow
moatNotes: API access, connector upkeep, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Planable because the scheduler is easy; staying approved and correct across constantly changing social APIs is the subscription. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Active open-source social media scheduling platform.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Draft, comment, approve and publish from shared workspaces; the free hosted plan does not meter collaborators.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean does not yet match Planable's polished per-network mockups, revision history and fine-grained approval states.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Team drafts, comments and publishing in one place; approval workflow is serviceable rather than ceremonial.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz's approval workflow is more basic than Planable's review-centric product, and self-hosting adds operational work.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: TryPost
alternatives.desc: Roles, comments, approvals and a visual calendar; the software is free, the server is yours.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or production Docker Compose; a bare-metal installation is also documented.
facts.engines: AI writing can use OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the deployment template also exposes Anthropic and Gemini keys.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL or MySQL stores app data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media is local or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: TryPost offers comments and approvals but lacks Planable's highly refined previews, revision history and client-review experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a SQL database, Redis, media storage, and separate developer credentials for each social platform.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a single-network scheduler DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Planable in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one official social-platform API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: draft social posts collaboratively, preview them accurately, approve them before publishing manually or through one official API, and retain a searchable content calendar.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support drafts, scheduled times, queues, campaigns, tags, and a weekly calendar.
Connect exactly one social network using its documented OAuth flow.
Validate character, media, aspect-ratio, and file-size limits before scheduling.
Publish through an idempotent background job with retries and clear failure states.
Store platform post identifiers and refresh publication status without scraping.
Add reusable snippets, local media storage, CSV export, and a token reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out unofficial automation or scraping.
Deliberately leave out multi-network inbox and social listening.
Deliberately leave out agency approvals, white labelling, and enterprise reporting.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
